title: Agents need more than a chat - Jacob Lauritzen, CTO Legora
talk_summary: Jacob Lauritzen argues that for long-running complex agents the bottleneck has shifted from doing work to planning and reviewing it, and that chat is a poor low-bandwidth interface for steering that work. He lays out concrete levers to raise trust (verifiability, guardrails, decomposition) and control (skills, elicitation with decision logs, high-bandwidth artifacts like documents and tabular reviews).

takeaways.technique: Make tasks verifiable to enable agent self-correction loops
takeaways.what_they_do: They push tasks down the verifiability spectrum (browser access, TDD, golden-reference comparisons, linting-style checks) so an agent can be run in a loop and told what it did wrong until it converges.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can make a task verifiable, you can just run an agent in a loop and tell it, "Hey, you did this wrong. Please fix it."

takeaways.technique: Skills encode human judgment at work nodes, with contingencies
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one big plan, they attach reusable 'skills' to specific sub-tasks (e.g. how to review confidentiality clauses, special EU termination law) so the agent handles special cases as it encounters them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the skills allow you to encode human judgment into essentially the nodes of work

takeaways.technique: Elicitation with decision log instead of blocking
takeaways.what_they_do: When the agent is unsure it makes a decision itself, unblocks, and writes the decision to a log the human reviews afterward and can reverse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make a decision, unblock yourself, but write this to a decision log

takeaways.what_they_do: They collaborate with agents through durable artifacts (documents, tabular reviews) where humans can highlight, comment, tag agents, and hand off sub-parts, instead of a linear chat that collapses the work tree.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Chat is one-dimensional. It's a very low bandwidth interface, and it tries to collapse this work tree into a single sort of linear thing.

takeaways.what_they_do: They raise trust by limiting what an agent can touch: only certain files, directories, or websites, rather than full access or per-action approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can only edit these three files, you can only read these from this directory, you can only search these websites

takeaways.technique: Decompose tasks and reserve human judgment for unverifiable parts
takeaways.what_they_do: They split a big task into verifiable sub-tasks (formatting, definition linting) and leave judgment-heavy choices (risk profile, precedent selection, negotiation stance) to humans.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can turn that from one task into a bunch of other tasks, and I can leave picking a risk profile... to the human
